papers.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
papers.abstract: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $\Omega_\epsilon(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-\epsilon}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<\epsilon<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit. As applications, we obtain two nearly optimal magic state protocols: CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent $\gamma \rightarrow 0$ and error suppression of nearly linear order, and a magic state fountain that directly prepares $N^{1-\epsilon}$ encoded CCZ magic states with nearly linear distance $\Omega_\epsilon(N/\log^2N)$. The construction uses balanced products of expanding graph covers. The assumption concerns Reed--Solomon codes on three subfields of characteristic two and pairwise coprime extension degrees, a local hypothesis studied in a companion manuscript. We design the expanding graph covers to admit many common classical codewords, which yield logical operators whose pairings select the logical CCZ gates independently. Without the product expansion assumption, the graph covers also yield classical LDPC codes over a fixed field with almost linear dimension and linear distance that satisfy a multiplication property: the coordinatewise product of any three codewords lies in a second LDPC code of linear distance.

papers.title: A Characterization of Rings Where a Linear Transformation and Its Inverse and Transpose Have the Same Information Exchange
papers.abstract: Linear transformations are considered over finite commutative rings. It is shown that the information exchange of an invertible linear transformation and that of its inverse are equal for any ring. It is also shown that the information exchange of any linear transformation and that of its transpose are equal if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications are presented to the Discrete Fourier Transform, to the analysis of Vandermonde transformations, and to area-time complexity.

papers.title: A slightly improved upper bound for quantum statistical zero-knowledge
papers.abstract: The complexity class Quantum Statistical Zero-Knowledge ($\mathsf{QSZK}$), introduced by Watrous (FOCS 2002) and later refined in Watrous (SICOMP, 2009), has the best known upper bound $\mathsf{QIP(2)} \cap \text{co-}\mathsf{QIP(2)}$, which was simplified following the inclusion $\mathsf{QIP(2)} \subseteq \mathsf{PSPACE}$ established in Jain, Upadhyay, and Watrous (FOCS 2009). Here, $\mathsf{QIP(2)}$ denotes the class of promise problems that admit two-message quantum interactive proof systems in which the honest prover is typically computationally unbounded, and $\text{co-}\mathsf{QIP(2)}$ denotes the complement of $\mathsf{QIP(2)}$. We slightly improve this upper bound to $\mathsf{QIP(2)} \cap \text{co-}\mathsf{QIP(2)}$ with a quantum linear-space honest prover. Specifically, the honest prover uses space linear in the size of the transcript of the original $\mathsf{QSZK}$ proof system. A similar improvement also applies to the upper bound for the non-interactive variant $\mathsf{NIQSZK}$. Our main techniques are algorithmic versions of the Holevo-Helstrom measurement and the Uhlmann transform, both implementable in quantum linear space, implying polynomial-time complexity in the state dimension, using the recent space-efficient quantum singular value transformation of Le Gall, Liu, and Wang (CC, 2026). We also establish that our linear-space bounds for these two tasks are near-optimal under the counting version of the Satisfiability Hypothesis (#SH).

papers.title: Brownian Bridge Diffusion-Assisted Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection for Jamming-Resilient OFDM Receivers
papers.abstract: In next-generation wireless networks, the growing density of devices and limited spectrum resources pose severe jamming challenges to fragile legitimate communication links in the wireless electromagnetic environment. Crucially, when jamming overlaps with pilot and data symbols in both time and frequency domains, it inflicts a severe bottleneck on receiver-side joint estimation and detection. Existing schemes often lack an effective framework to combat such jamming contamination, thereby failing to guarantee reliable transmission. To address this issue, we propose a Brownian bridge diffusion-assisted joint channel estimation and data detection (BBD-JCED) framework for jamming-resilient orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) receivers. The proposed framework consists of a jamming suppression module and a Brownian bridge-joint recovery module. The former identifies jamming-contaminated bins in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain and suppresses the dominant jamming components through spectral notching. The latter establishes a Brownian bridge-based probabilistic graph to model the probabilistic transition process from the suppressed OFDM observation to the coded bits, and performs a reverse recovery process to enable enhanced joint channel estimation and data detection. Moreover, we derive a variational lower bound (VLB) to reformulate the intractable bit estimate problem into a tractable training objective, providing a probabilistic foundation for the loss function design. Furthermore, we develop a two-stage training algorithm to separately optimize the jamming suppression and Brownian bridge-joint recovery modules. Simulation results under representative jamming types demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior jamming suppression and bit recovery performance over the considered baseline schemes while maintaining competitive inference complexity.

papers.title: A Geometric Coding Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a direct analogue of the classical Coding Theorem in the setting of symmetry groups. We consider computable bijections on the set of binary strings and define the symmetry prior of a string x as the probability that a randomly chosen symmetry from a given group G has x as its unique fixed point. We show that for any fix-retractable symmetry group G, a group admitting a computable section that selects an isolating symmetry for every string, the symmetry prior is a universal lower semi-computable semi-measure. In this case, the Geometric Coding Theorem holds. This result is a coding-theoretic restatement of a theorem of Trejo, Kreinovich and Longpr\'e, who showed that the complexity of describing a string by a symmetry with that string as its unique fixed point equals its Kolmogorov complexity. Our contribution is to recast it in terms of algorithmic probability and to treat the symmetry group as a parameter, identifying fix-retractability as exactly the condition under which symmetry complexity collapses onto Kolmogorov complexity.

papers.title: Orbits as Strong Models: Kolmogorov Structure Function under Symmetry
papers.abstract: Strong models in algorithmic statistics are essentially the cells of simple partitions of $\{0,1\}^n$. We study the partitions that come from symmetry, the orbit partitions of groups acting on strings, and the structure function $h^G_x$ they induce. A set is a cell of such a partition exactly when its setwise stabiliser acts transitively on it, so $h^G_x$ is Kolmogorov's structure function restricted to $G$-homogeneous sets. For the full symmetric group this recovers all models and exactly the strong ones. For $GL(n,2)$ the cells are the linearly homogeneous sets, $h^{GL}_x$ lies in a band between $C(x)-\alpha$ and $n-\alpha$ with both edges attained, and some stochastic normal strings have simple structure that is invisible to linear symmetry. Writing each permutation group as a Burnside-ring type with a placement, we show that any space of symmetry hypotheses small enough to search is small enough to miss simple structure. Finally we cast the search for orbit models as value estimation on subgroup lattices, with computable bounds, certified training targets and a lattice version of Monte Carlo tree search.

papers.title: Efficiency of ANS Entropy Encoders
papers.abstract: Asymmetric Numeral Systems (ANS) is a class of entropy encoders that had an immense impact on the data compression, substituting arithmetic and Huffman coding. It was studied by different authors but the precise asymptotics of its redundancy (in relation to the entropy) was not completely understood. We obtain optimal bounds for the redundancy of the tabled ANS (tANS), the most popular ANS variant. Given a sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ of symbols from an alphabet $\{0,1,\ldots,\sigma-1\}$ such that each symbol $a$ occurs in it $f_a$ times and $n=2^r$, the tANS encoder using Duda's ``precise initialization'' to fill tANS tables transforms this sequence into a bit string of the following length (the frequencies are not included in the encoding): $\sum\limits_{a\in[0..\sigma)}f_a\cdot\log\frac{n}{f_a}+O(\sigma+r)$, where $O(\sigma+r)$ can be bounded by $\sigma\log e+r$. The $r$-bit term is an artifact indispensable to ANS; the rest incurs a redundancy of $O(\frac{\sigma}{n})$ bits per symbol. We complement this by examples showing that an $\Omega(\sigma+r)$ redundancy is necessary. We argue that similar examples exist for most adequate initialization methods for tANS. Thus, we refute Duda's conjecture that the redundancy is $O(\frac{\sigma}{n^2})$ bits per symbol. We also propose a variant of the range ANS (rANS), called rANS with fixed accuracy, parameterized by $k\ge 1$ that in certain conditions might be faster than the standard rANS because it avoids slow explicit division operations. We bound the redundancy for our rANS variant by $\frac{n}{2^k-1}\log e+r+k$.

papers.title: $p$-ary (Non Weakly) Regular Bent Functions in Generalized $\cPS$ class
papers.abstract: We use $m$-dimensional partial spreads of $\fp^{2n}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $n$ is a positive integer and $m$ divides $n$, to construct two classes of bent functions from $\fp^{2n}$ to $\fp$. Our construction generalizes the classes of $p$-ary $\cPS^{-}$ and $\cPS^{+}$ regular bent functions proposed by P. Lison\v ek and H. Y. Lu (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 73 (2014), 209--216). Unlike the original class, such bent functions can be either regular or non weakly regular.

papers.title: Shared Randomness and Parallel Rounds in Permutation Sampling
papers.abstract: Sampling a uniformly random permutation of $[n]$ in parallel is a coordination problem: $n$ processors, one per coordinate, must output distinct values. A single round requires a shared seed of $\log n!$ nats, while $n$ rounds require no shared randomness. We determine the tradeoff in between for $R$ rounds, in which the values of each round are written independently given the shared randomness and the earlier output, and the output must be a uniform permutation, exactly or within total-variation error $\varepsilon$. Shared randomness is measured by its support size or by its entropy, and it is either fixed in advance or drawn adaptively during the execution. For exact sampling, all four costs equal one explicit combinatorial quantity up to an absolute additive constant. A fixed error $0<\varepsilon<1$ shortens the seed by $O(1)$ nats in one round, where the least number of seed values, an approximate nonnegative tensor rank, is $(1-3\varepsilon/2)\,n!$ up to an additive two for $\varepsilon\le1/2$. The saving is $\Theta((\log n)^2)$ nats in two rounds, with a sharp constant, and of lower order for $R=o(n)$; for $R\sim\rho n$ with $0<\rho<1$ it is linear in $n$, with the optimal rate given by a variational formula. Here, errors above an explicit threshold need only $o(n)$ nats, and at every positive error below it, shared randomness drawn adaptively has strictly smaller entropy than a seed fixed in advance. A central tool is a change of measure that turns lower bounds with error into entropy bounds for a single batch of distinct, nearly independent values. The results for sublinearly and linearly many rounds extend to sampling without replacement.

papers.title: The Double Entropy Fit Index (DEFI): An Information-Theoretic Approach to Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering
authors: Gabriel Lawrence (Department of Systems and Information Engineering
Daniel Otero-Leon (Department of Systems and Information Engineering & Department of Public Health Sciences
papers.abstract: We introduce the Double-Entropy Fit Index (DEFI), a regularized information-theoretic criterion for selecting among candidate graph partitions and reduced representations. DEFI couples entropy-based compression with relevance preservation and penalizes model dimensionality, cluster imbalance, and partition fragmentation. An exact R\'enyi-2 entropy identity shows that partitioning alters both spectral concentration and graph-volume normalization, explaining why unregularized entropy minimization can favor degenerate solutions. Across a 243-condition population-analytic factor recovery benchmark, DEFI achieved an overall exact recovery rate of 97.2\% (versus 75.0\% for EGA-TMFG, 45.8\% for TEFI on von Neumann entropy). In controlled local candidate batteries (distinguishing the true model from adjacent $K \pm 1$ and factor-split alternatives), DEFI identified the correct partition in 99.2\% of replications. Across ten clustering benchmarks, DEFI-guided Gaussian mixtures achieved a mean ARI of 0.929, exceeding HDBSCAN (0.809), Ward clustering (0.700), and conventional GMM criteria (0.501-0.580), with gains concentrating where standard criteria over-extract components.

papers.title: Drift-Aware Adaptive Semantic Codec Update Strategy for Dynamic Semantic Communications
papers.abstract: Semantic communication reduces transmission overhead by conveying task-relevant semantic features, but its performance depends on the consistency between training and target-domain data distributions. In dynamic environments, distribution drift can make offline-trained semantic codec models stale and degrade transmission performance. Frequent updates alleviate this degradation but increase communication, computation, and queueing costs, whereas infrequent updates delay model adaptation. To address this tradeoff, we propose a drift-aware adaptive update strategy for dynamic semantic communication systems. Drift intensity is quantified in the semantic feature space, and Drift-Aware Age of Model (DA-AoM) is introduced to jointly capture drift-induced performance degradation, drift-dependent update service delay, and conventional update latency. Closed-form average DA-AoM expressions are derived for edge-layer M/M/1 and cloud-layer D/M/1 update scenarios, based on which the update frequency is optimized under the queueing-stability constraint. Simulations show that DA-AoM captures the joint effects of drift intensity, computing rate, bandwidth, and update frequency on model freshness beyond conventional Age of Information (AoI). The proposed strategy reduces average DA-AoM by 9.2\%--42.4\% compared with representative baselines under the same resource constraints.

papers.title: The Geometry of Mode Sampling in Reconfigurable MIMO Channel Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays acquire channels by distributing radiation modes across their antenna elements. Equal mode counts fix the observation budget while leaving a spatial sampling choice that directly affects reconstruction of unmeasured channels. We establish how this assignment enters the inverse problem through the receive aperture and the coupling between propagation paths. For an isolated path with calibrated positive real responses, the power-weighted variance of antenna positions completely characterizes the assignment dependence of the profiled angle information at fixed mode counts. We then construct layouts with identical weighted apertures and different path correlations, exposing a limitation of aperture-based design in multipath propagation. A paired simulation study evaluates balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling using a common estimator with per-detection joint angle refinement. Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are entirely unobserved, with improvements across nearly all tested scenes at high signal-to-noise ratio. When every mode is sampled, the mean benefit is more sensitive to rare large errors. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the spatial distribution of mode measurements to both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.

papers.title: Benchmarking Traditional and Learning-Based Reference-Free Compressors for Long-Read Sequencing Data
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies generate large volumes of data, creating substantial storage and transmission demands. Although reference-based compressors can achieve high compression, their reliance on an appropriate reference genome limits their use. We present LRCBench, a benchmark and survey of reference-free lossless compressors for long-read sequencing data. We review traditional and learning-based general-purpose and sequencing-specific methods, then evaluate 35 compressors on 16 real-world datasets from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio platforms. We compare compression ratio, storage savings, runtime, peak memory use, and robustness across datasets. Learning-based compressors are evaluated on six MinION datasets because of their high computational costs. CoLoRd achieves the best overall compression ratios in our experiments, while other methods offer trade-offs in speed, memory use, and robustness. We also examine multithreaded speedup and discuss future directions in parallel acceleration, privacy protection, adaptive parameter tuning, and hardware-algorithm co-design.

papers.title: SFiD: Self-Supervised Fitness-Driven Optimization for Next-Generation Networking
papers.abstract: Next-generation (NG) wireless networks face increasingly complex and dynamic optimization challenges driven by data-intensive applications and massive device connectivity. Existing methods suffer from one or more limitations, including high computational complexity, poor scalability and adaptability, reliance on large labeled datasets, or weak generalization in dynamic and non-convex wireless environments. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a self-supervised fitness-driven diffusion (SFiD) method that autonomously generates its own training data and iteratively learns from it. It also exhibits strong generalization capabilities and the ability to effectively tackle challenging optimization problems. We validate the convergence of our proposed method to the global optimum on both analytical convex and non-convex optimization problems. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we consider reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) phaseshift optimization in cell-free massive multiple-input multipleoutput (CF-mMIMO) systems with imperfect channel state information and spatial correlation at the RIS as a case study. Specifically, we develop SFiD-C for continuous variable optimization and apply it to optimize continuous RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. We also develop SFiD-D for discrete variable optimization and apply it to optimize discrete RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. Furthermore, we develop a binary neural network (BNN) based version of SFiDD for reducing its computational complexity, referred to as SFiD-D (BNN). Finally, our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods markedly improve computational efficiency and achieve comparable or superior performance compared to meta-heuristic and DRL benchmarks for both continuous and discrete RIS phase-shift optimization.

papers.title: MIMO Channel Extrapolation to Unobserved Radiation Modes via Learned Path Refinement
papers.abstract: A pattern-reconfigurable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver can sample every antenna element and still leave entire radiation modes unobserved. The calibrated patterns weight a common set of propagation paths, which links these missing channels to the measured rows. Our estimator learns to correct the complex gains and spatial frequencies of those paths, so a correction inferred from measured rows updates every unmeasured mode. Each stage combines a damped least-squares proposal with a learned correction scaled by noise power and local array sensitivity. Training on complete simulated channels rewards corrections that reduce prediction error across modes, including those with no measured rows. The learned rule transfers from pursuit-based training estimates to a ridge variable-projection initializer without retraining. In matched simulations, refinement reduces error on wholly unobserved modes as well as across the full channel. Coefficient updates account for most of the gain, and the learned rule further improves on adaptive ridge shrinkage at fixed angles. Individual channel trajectories show that extrapolation can improve even as the residual on the measured rows increases.

papers.title: Construction of Ternary Minimal Linear Codes with Dimension $n+r$ Via Index Codes and The Access Structures of Their Dual Codes
papers.abstract: Recently, minimal linear codes have been extensively studied due to their applications in secret sharing schemes, secure two-party computations, and so on. Constructing minimal linear codes violating the Ashikhmin-Barg condition and then determining their weight distributions have been interesting in coding theory and cryptography. In this paper, we present a general construction of ternary linear codes of dimension $n+r$, where $n$ and $r$ are positive integers, and derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the resulting codes to be minimal. We first specialize the construction using index codes arising from spreads, with three classes of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters and weight enumerators of the corresponding minimal codes, and determine the access structures type of the secret-sharing schemes based on their dual codes. By the index codes from Krawtchouk polynomials, we then give a second specialization of the construction, with a class of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters of the resulting minimal codes, and determine the access-structure type of the secret-sharing scheme based on each dual code. Several constructed families of minimal codes violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

papers.title: Continuous Noisy-Loop Models
papers.abstract: Efficient learning and inference need not imply a compact probabilistic circuit. We quantify this distinction for continuous noisy readings of agreement between adjacent latent spins on a known square grid with $d$ edges. With known margins and bounded Lipschitz channels, minimax squared Hellinger risk is $\Theta(\min\{1,dN^{-2/3}\})$ from $N$ independent vectors, without a reliability lower bound. A spline estimator reaches this rate in polynomial arithmetic time given a fixed positive reliability bound; an exponential-size mixture removes that requirement. At fixed positive reliability, nonnegative decomposable circuits need $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt d))$ nodes for fixed total-variation error below one, even when each leaf uses at most $\alpha d$ coordinates, $0<\alpha<1$. Optimal Kullback--Leibler (KL) approximation error is $\Theta(d/\max\{\log d,\sqrt\ell\})$ in either direction with at most $d^r$ nodes and leaf scopes $\ell\leq\alpha d$, for fixed $r>1$ and $0<\alpha<2/3$. Node counts exclude leaf computation. For three fixed masks, optimal joint conditional KL has order $d/\log d$ when $\ell\leq(\log d)^2$. Local cycle identities relate joint divergence to identifiable channel products and separate weak-channel recovery from density estimation. Factorized evidence preserves a planar zero-field Ising model: given local integrals, exact queries cost $O(d^{3/2})$ arithmetic operations and one root extraction.

papers.title: Rational v. Radical: Trajectory Properties of Iterated Bayesian Updates
papers.abstract: Iterating Jeffrey's update on fixed evidence gives a maximum-likelihood estimate under suitable support conditions. What is less clear would be how the trajectories are organized, and what happens when we trace them in reverse. For a fixed strictly positive, invertible classical channel and full-support evidence, reverse iteration corresponds to repeated prior hacking. Almost every interior prior then approaches certainty in one possibility while each nontrivial step worsens agreement with the evidence. We call this limiting behavior radicalization. Priors that approach the same pure state form a Bayes phase. In the phase diagrams, the separating trajectories instead approach facet fixed points determined by M-projections. We also ask whether one can choose evidence that brings every interior prior to the same conclusion. For a strictly positive, invertible channel this is always possible, although one cannot always prescribe which conclusion it will be

papers.title: Hull variation of algebraic geometry codes under divisor twists
papers.abstract: The hull $\mathrm{Hull}(\mathcal{C})=\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{C}^{\perp}$ of a linear code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ interpolates between linear complementary dual (LCD) codes, with trivial hull, and self-dual codes. Its dimension is preserved by coordinate permutations but not by scalings $\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathbf{x}\cdot\mathcal{C}$, $\mathbf{x}\in(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^n$. This governs the complexity of Sendrier's support-splitting algorithm and decides whether an equivalence class contains LCD codes. We study this hull-variation problem, formalised by Chen, for algebraic geometry codes $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ over a function field $\mathcal{F}/\mathbb{F}_q$ of genus $g>0$, where scalings are twists of $G$ by principal divisors; as a natural relaxation, we allow twists $G\mapsto G+L$ by arbitrary divisors. Writing $\mathcal{C}(D,G)^{\perp}=\mathcal{C}(D,H)$, with $H=D-G+W$, $W$ canonical, a twist acts by $(G,H)\mapsto(G+L,H-L)$. Whenever $\gcd(G+L,H-L)$ is non-special, the hull dimensions of $\mathcal{C}(D,G+L)$ and $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ differ by exactly $\frac12(\mathrm{deg}|G-H|-\mathrm{deg}|G-H+2L|)$. For a genuine scaling, $L=-(z)$, this variation is bounded by $2[\mathcal{F}:\mathbb{F}_q(z)]$. Under the same hypothesis, we obtain an upper bound on the hull dimension depending only on $D$ and $W$, and characterise exactly when it is attained by a scaling of it. These bounds shed new light on Chen's maximal hull dimension; explicit scalings on Kummer extensions show that the first is sharp. We construct explicit twists that raise, respectively lower, the hull dimension by prescribed amounts, one unit at a time, and apply them to two classical families. Starting from known LCD codes, we reach every hull dimension in an explicit range; starting from a self-dual code ($q$ even) or a code of maximal hull dimension ($q$ odd), we descend to $0$, yielding LCD codes of various dimensions.

papers.title: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Exact Bounds and Extremizers
papers.abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy $D(P\|Q)$ in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences $\chi^2(P\|Q)$ and $\chi^2(Q\|P)$. For any $A,B>0$, the constraints $\chi^2(P\|Q)\leq A$ and $\chi^2(Q\|P)\leq B$ yield upper bounds on $D(P\|Q)$ and $D(Q\|P)$. Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions each attain both bounds simultaneously. As a consequence, for sequences of probability mass functions $\{P_n\}$ and $\{Q_n\}$ on a common finite or countably infinite alphabet, both $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ and $D(Q_n\|P_n)$ tend to zero whenever one of the two ordered chi-squared divergences tends to zero and the other remains uniformly bounded. Without this boundedness assumption, $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ can fail to converge to zero even when $\chi^2(Q_n\|P_n)\to 0$. Finally, in contrast to the attainable upper bounds, on any finite or countably infinite alphabet containing at least three elements, the infimum of $D(P\|Q)$ under the exact constraints $\chi^2(P\|Q)=A$ and $\chi^2(Q\|P)=B$ is zero and is not attained.

papers.title: The Asymptotic Capacity of the Grabbag Channel With and Without Feedback
papers.abstract: The grabbag channel models communication through a randomly mixed store. At each use, an input ball of one of $K$ colors is inserted into a bag containing $M$ balls, and one of the resulting $M+1$ balls is selected uniformly, observed, and removed. We show that, when $2\leq K\leq M+1$, both the capacity without feedback and the capacity with noiseless strictly causal output feedback are at most $9.77(K/(M+1))^{2/3}$, and that, when moreover $M+1\geq2^{22}$, both are at least an absolute constant times $(K/(M+1))^{2/3}$. Hence, both capacities are of order $(K/M)^{2/3}$, and of order $M^{-2/3}$ for every fixed $K$. The converse is a single bound on the information that a feedback code conveys in $n$ uses, valid for every initial state. For each initial state, it bounds the information in each output by the change of a potential of the posterior law of the state given the earlier outputs, defined through noisy cube roots of the color counts. A budget on the true state bounds the total cost of the uses in which the inserted color is rare. The lower bound uses a statistic of two output histograms whose expectation does not depend on the unknown initial composition, an outer code, and words with prescribed compositions. We also show that the channel is indecomposable and relate its capacities to the finite-state-channel information formulas.

papers.title: On cyclic codes generated by cyclotomic polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $n$ be a composite positive integer coprime to $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and let $t = \operatorname{lpf}(n)$ be the least prime factor of $n$. In this paper we study the cyclic codes $\mathcal{C}_{n,t} = \langle Q_n(X)Q_t(X)\rangle$ and $\mathcal{C}_{n,t,1} = \langle Q_n(X)Q_t(X)Q_1(X)\rangle$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $Q_d(X)$ denotes the $d$-th cyclotomic polynomial. These codes extend the families $\mathcal{C}_n = \langle Q_n(X)\rangle$ and $\mathcal{C}_{n,1} = \langle Q_n(X)Q_1(X)\rangle$ recently studied by Bhagat and Sarma. We determine the exact minimum distances of $\mathcal{C}_{n,t}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{n,t,1}$, showing that $d(\mathcal{C}_{n,t,1}) = 2t$ and that $d(\mathcal{C}_{n,t})$ equals $t$ if $t^2 \nmid n$, and $2t$ if $t^2 \mid n$. For the dual codes, we establish $d(\mathcal{C}_{n,t}^\perp) = 2^{\omega(n)}$, handling the case $\omega(n) \le 2$ via the Hartmann--Tzeng bound, and the case $\omega(n) \ge 3$ via a direct-sum decomposition $\mathcal{C}_{n,t}^\perp = \mathcal{C}_n^\perp \oplus \mathcal{V}_t$ and the tensor-product structure of $\mathcal{C}_n^\perp$ over its prime-power components. As applications, we show that all four code families are linear complementary dual (LCD) and locally recoverable (LRC), and we determine their locality parameters, identifying several infinite families that are $r$-optimal or $d$-optimal with respect to the Singleton-type bound for LRC codes.

papers.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL
papers.abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. To eliminate the risks of explicit exploration, we then introduce Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration (PF-EFVI), a purely greedy algorithm that leverages reward diversity to ensure state-action coverage. We prove that PF-EFVI attains logarithmic regret without explicit exploration bonuses under sufficient reward diversity. Our results reveal that agent disagreement shifts the exploration burden from temporal complexity to spatial diversity, enabling efficient collective learning without explicit exploration.

papers.title: A Differential Theory of Quality-Resource Trade-offs for AI Model Selection: The Multiresource Frontier and Its Minimax Price
papers.abstract: Comparing AI models across resource budgets yields quality-resource frontiers relating error to latency, parameter count, training compute, and energy. Offset power laws summarize such frontiers, but their fitted parameters reveal neither the price-independent geometry nor the manner in which trade-offs extend across several resource channels. This paper addresses both gaps by developing a differential theory in which this structure is made explicit. Each frontier admits a price-independent plane-curve representation relating the effective number of active resource channels, $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = s^2/\kappa$ (squared slope over curvature), to the remaining log-error depth, $\Delta S = \ln(\varepsilon/\varepsilon_{\infty})$. This representation separates intrinsic shape from the scale and origin of the resource axis. Complete monotonicity and divisibility yield differential inequalities and frontier bounds. When each of $N$ resources contributes one active channel, the theory gives the parameter-free operating rule $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1$ in delivered units and derives minimax resource prices $\lambda^{\star}_i = \alpha_i/(N+1)$ with an exact worst-case regret of $\ln(N+1)$ nats. The results make it possible to interpret measured frontiers and compare resource costs without hand-chosen exchange rates. The theory is evaluated on 117 published frontiers and implemented in the open-source package nn-rank, which derives prices from measured quality and cost, ranks candidates, and reports supported choices and minimax regret: https://github.com/ABrain-One/nn-rank

papers.title: Electromagnetic Channel Model and Sensing Performance for ISAC: The Case of a Single Cylindrical Scatterer
papers.abstract: We propose an electromagnetic wireless channel model for accurate target localization in radar-like sensing scenarios. The model employs a self-consistent method grounded in wave scattering theory and imposing boundary conditions, providing the (impedance) channel transfer matrix for a propagation channel with a single target modeled as a cylindrical scatterer. The model is: 1) physics-based, as it includes electromagnetic interactions between objects; 2) unified, as it is valid in both near- and far-field regions. Within the canonical two-dimensional and 2.5-dimensional configurations with line-source and dipole-source excitations, respectively, the model supports dielectric cylinders with frequency-dependent permittivity. Localization accuracy is assessed via the Cramer-Rao lower bound for a dielectric cylinder with variable position, radius, and dielectric constant. Provisions for future extensions to extended targets are discussed in the context of 3GPP channel modeling.

papers.title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
papers.abstract: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it. We say that the setting covers those observables. We determine how many random settings cover a prescribed fraction of all Pauli observables. As the number of settings grows exponentially with the number of qubits, the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of $3^{3/4}$ per qubit, set by the rate-distortion function of covering at zero distortion. We give an explicit expression for the number of settings needed to reach a target fraction, accurate up to a remainder that reduces to a small oscillation for many qubits, and show that random sampling is asymptotically optimal up to a factor of less than 1.69. Coverage does not determine what a setting contributes to an estimator. Observables covered by one setting are estimated from the same outcomes, so their estimates are correlated. We quantify this correlation through the design effect of a setting, which equals the squared Pauli expectation that the setting captures and depends on the target state. We derive its mean over settings in closed form for every state and show that it can be estimated without bias from the measurement data. In simulations on six qubits, measuring settings needs 7.6 to 38 times fewer circuit runs than measuring the same number of observables independently. At high coverage, fitting the outcome histograms instead of averaged estimates roughly halves the reconstruction error, mainly because the fit counts how many settings cover each observable. The correlation itself costs such a fit about a factor of two, and a larger design effect signals more to gain from modeling it.

papers.title: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.

papers.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

papers.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
papers.abstract: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. First, we establish the S-SM-NR framework by formulating the joint design of the task graph and the transmit-listen schedule. Then, we analyze the minimum round count required by S-SM-NR and establish a connectivity condition for network localization. Subsequently, we develop a closed-form joint design that constructs the sparse task graph and the balanced transmit-listen schedule. In particular, the joint design can achieve the minimum round count under the complete physical connectivity. Finally, simulations show that the proposed S-SM-NR scheme reduces the occupied-round count and improves the localization accuracy by shortening the ranging cycle.

papers.title: Semifields and rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Drinfeld modules and rank-metric codes, focusing on maximum rank distance codes arising from finite semifields. Our method constructs rank-metric codes from linear subspaces of endomorphisms of a Drinfeld module acting on torsion submodules. Using a duality between a Drinfeld module and its endomorphisms, we show that Sheekey's construction fits naturally into this framework, yielding a short conceptual proof of his main theorem. Next, to demonstrate the potential of our method, we construct, for every prime power $q$, new semifields of order $q^9$, which are distinguished from the known ones by their nuclear parameters. Finally, going beyond the Drinfeld module $\phi_T=\tau^n$ that underlies Sheekey's and related constructions, we obtain infinite families of semifield codes from Drinfeld modules with smaller endomorphism rings, and show that the corresponding semifields are cyclic semifields of Petit.
